$comment: Neutral guardrail-hook SSOT for this repo — the hooks half of Argo's cross-CLI setup (skills are skills-lock.json's half). One entry per behavior; `packages/argo-skills/bin/hooks-sync.mts` projects them into each harness named in `agents` below: claude-code -> .claude/settings.json, codex -> .codex/hooks.json. Never hand-edit those generated blocks — edit here and run `bun run hooks:sync`. Commands are harness-neutral: `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/packages/argo-skills/skills/setup-argo-skills/hooks/*` (no $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR). The commands invoke that path via git-toplevel; a consumer opts in by hand, copying this file AND that directory into its own tree before projecting there. `setup-argo-skills` carries the steps; nothing installs them for you. Optional top-level `prOwnershipGuard.publishBranches` names branch namespaces any agent may push without `/ship`. `worktreeGc.artifactPaths` is read by the manual `bun run worktrees:sweep`, not by a hook.

hooks.$comment: PR ownership: `/ship` is the only skill that pushes a work branch or opens a pull request (#1669). A PreToolUse hook cannot tell which skill is running - Claude Code's payload carries no field naming the active skill and no environment variable does either - so this cannot deny "unless the skill is ship". It denies the action outright and takes an explicit opt-out instead: a command carrying the `ARGO_SHIP=1` environment prefix is allowed through, and `ship/SKILL.md` writes that prefix into the commands it tells the agent to run. The marker is part of the command line, so what claimed the exemption is visible in the transcript. Three shapes are allowed unmarked, none of them a work branch: a push that deletes a ref, a push targeting a ref outside refs/heads/ (the PNG evidence ref), and a push to a branch under one of `prOwnershipGuard.publishBranches` (the design page, which joins to no ticket and which `/ship` has no step for).

The to-do-list nudge. AGENTS.md carries the same rule, but a rule that competes with a whole file for attention is one sessions skip: measured over 2981 transcripts, only 38% of sessions with three or more file edits wrote a list at all, and the rate fell over time (#1254). The script reads the session's own transcript and goes quiet the moment a list exists, and gives up after three prompts either way. It only ever adds context — it can never block a prompt.
